title: POC Weekly - Caching Sync
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on caching metrics and prompt reuse strategy. Reviewed prefix cache hit rates (overall ~42%) and KV cache effectiveness (~68%) across three main routes. Identified prompt churn as main hit-rate limiter - many prompts slightly differ (timestamps, PII redaction) causing cache misses. Agreed to 1) canonicalize prompt templates and whitespace/metadata stripping, 2) instrument per-model/per-route hit-rate dashboards, 3) run an A/B test of aggressive TTL vs conservative TTL on a shadow workload to measure quality regressions. Next week goal: increase prefix cache hit to 55% and KV hit to 75% on health-insights route, plus share 1k canonical prompts from Acme for offline sim. Action items assigned and timeline agreed.
topics: KV cache hit rate and eviction policy
action_items: Priya (Redwood SE): Add per-model + per-route cache hit dashboards to shared Grafana (or Console) - due 2025-03-18
Jared (Acme): Export 1,000 representative prompts / user messages (anonymized) for offline replay - due 2025-03-13
Alex (Redwood AE): Send pricing note for Dedicated vs Hosted caching + cost delta estimates - due 2025-03-14
Sana (Acme Platform): Share current preprocessing pipeline rules (redaction, timestamp formatting) - due 2025-03-13
Priya (Redwood SE): Run shadow A/B test with TTL 30s vs TTL 300s on health-insights route and report quality metrics - start 2025-03-14, initial results by 2025-03-21
next_steps: Set up shared Grafana dashboard and invite customer
Customer to provide sanitized prompt set for replay

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-11
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jared Mills (Head of ML - Acme), Sana Patel (Platform Eng - Acme), Luis Hernandez (PM - Acme)

Summary (auto): Quick sync on caching: prefix and K V cache hit rates, prompt reuse strategy, dashboards, and A/B test plan.

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we are on for the weekly caching sync. Quick roll call?
[00:00:06] Jared (Acme): Jared here, hi.
[00:00:08] Sana (Acme): Sana on the line.
[00:00:09] Luis (Acme): Luis - hi.
[00:00:11] Priya (Redwood): Priya here.
[00:00:13] Alex (Redwood): Sweet, okay so agenda: prefix cache numbers, K V cache, prompt canonicalization, TTL experiments, and dashboards. Priya you wanna kick off with numbers?
[00:00:23] Priya (Redwood): Yeah sure. So we ran the instrumented traces over the last seven days. Overall prefix cache hit across the three main routes is about forty two percent. The KV cache hit is roughly sixty eight percent, but that's concentrated on the patient-summary route. Health-insights route is lower, prefix hit is twenty eight percent there.
[00:00:44] Jared (Acme): Twenty eight's lower than I expected. Do we know why that's the case?
[00:00:48] Priya (Redwood): Two main things. One, prompt churn: the user prompt templates are similar but have lots of micro-variations - timestamps, user IDs, little punctuation differences. Two, our current preprocessing only normalizes whitespace, not all metadata. So small diffs end up as cache misses.
[00:01:04] Sana (Acme): To be clear, our upstream adds event timestamps and a session id in the first line, often in ISO. That alone will create unique prefixes almost every time.
[00:01:12] Priya (Redwood): Exactly. If we canonicalize the timestamp or strip it pre-cache key generation we can recover a lot of hits.
[00:01:18] Luis (Acme): Any rough idea of how much improvement canonicalization buys?
[00:01:22] Priya (Redwood): From our offline sim on a small sample, canonicalization + trimming metadata improved prefix hits from ~30% to ~54% on the same sample. But that's sampling, we'll need the customer prompt set to validate.
[00:01:33] Alex (Redwood): Also note there's a tradeoff - if you canonicalize too aggressively you could mask user-specific context and cause quality regressions. That's why we want to run a shadow A/B test.
[00:01:43] Jared (Acme): Right - we care about both latency/cost and accuracy. If caching breaks HIPAA-required redaction or misattributes info, that's a no-go.
[00:01:51] Priya (Redwood): Totally. Our plan: keep canonicalization rules conservative for now - strip timestamps, normalize common date formats, remove session IDs - but keep user identifiers that are semantically important. We'll log mismatches so we can iterate.
[00:02:03] Sana (Acme): What about TTL? Are we seeing evictions that are hurting hit rate?
[00:02:07] Priya (Redwood): Yes. Current default TTL is 60 seconds in the POC. For some routes where queries repeat quickly, that's fine. For others with bursty traffic it's suboptimal. In backlog test we saw increasing hit rate up to TTL 300s but with slight quality variance in the A/B.
[00:02:21] Alex (Redwood): So action: we'll run TTL 30s vs 300s shadow on health-insights to see both cost and quality delta. Priya you'll own that?
[00:02:28] Priya (Redwood): Yep I will kick that off. We'll run it as a shadow compare for two days then extend to a week if initial looks stable.
[00:02:35] Jared (Acme): Sounds good. What's the instrumentation look like? We need per-model, per-route metrics.
[00:02:41] Priya (Redwood): We'll surface metrics in the Redwood Console and push a Grafana dashboard. Key metrics: prefix_hit_rate, kv_hit_rate, tokens_saved, avg_latency, and a quality metric which is fuzzy-match similarity between cached output and full-run output in the shadow. We'll also report per-model breakdown and top N prefixes by misses.
[00:02:59] Luis (Acme): Can we get that exported to our internal monitoring? We use Datadog and Splunk.
[00:03:04] Priya (Redwood): Yep we can push events and metrics to Datadog. For logs Splunk can intake via the forwarder; we'll share the endpoint details.
[00:03:10] Alex (Redwood): Great. On cost: a quick note, caching tends to reduce token spend but increases memory/eviction pressure. For Dedicated vs Hosted there are different knobs - with Dedicated you get higher KV capacity per instance so better hit rate under same workload, but Reserved capacity pricing applies. I'll send a short note with cost delta.
[00:03:28] Jared (Acme): Please do. We're evaluating economics closely.
[00:03:31] Priya (Redwood): Also we noticed some mis-transcribed model names in the logs, e g 'Red wood dedicated' popped up in a few traces, probably transcription artifact - just ignore.
[00:03:41] Sana (Acme): (laughs) okay noted.
[00:03:43] Priya (Redwood): For prompt canonicalization, we proposed a two-step approach: offline replay with canonicalization to measure potential hit uplift, then live shadow A/B for quality. Offline replay requires the anonymized prompt set from Acme.
[00:03:58] Alex (Redwood): Jared, can you commit to sending a thousand prompts sanitized? That should be enough for a representative replay.
[00:04:05] Jared (Acme): I can do a 1k sample, yes. We'll strip PII and send encrypted to the shared S3 bucket.
[00:04:10] Luis (Acme): Timeline?
[00:04:11] Jared (Acme): I'll try to get it by Thursday 3/13.
[00:04:14] Priya (Redwood): Great. Once we have that, we run replay and produce a delta report: expected hit uplift and estimated token savings.
[00:04:22] Alex (Redwood): One more item - eviction policy. Right now it's LRU with a per-model cap. For some routes we might benefit from LFU or a hybrid to keep frequently used small prefixes. We can prototype a frequency-aware eviction for the health-insights route.
[00:04:36] Priya (Redwood): Agree. We'll try an LFU variant in the shadow bench. We'll document memory vs hit-rate tradeoffs.
[00:04:43] Sana (Acme): Any security concerns about caching PHI? We need assurance logs, audit trails, and optional encryption at rest.
[00:04:51] Alex (Redwood): Absolutely. For Private deployments we have KMS integrations; for Hosted we support customer-managed keys for encryption at rest for Dedicated. We'll share the security docs. Also audit logs for cache access are available in the Console.
[00:05:03] Jared (Acme): We'll need SOC2/ISO references and a short note on how long cached items live and how they're purged on request.
[00:05:10] Priya (Redwood): We'll attach the compliance sheet and a cache-purge playbook.
[00:05:14] Luis (Acme): On the quality metric you mentioned 'fuzzy-match similarity' - can you explain how that's computed?
[00:05:19] Priya (Redwood): It's a token-level edit-distance plus semantic similarity via embeddings threshold. It's not perfect but it flags large divergences to route for manual review.
[00:05:28] Alex (Redwood): Ok let's go through quick timeline recap and owners. Priya will add dashboards and run TTL A/B. Jared sends prompts by 3/13. Priya runs offline replay and reports. Alex sends pricing note by 3/14. Sana to share preprocessing rules.
[00:05:41] Jared (Acme): One last question - any competitor work we should know about? Are other vendors offering similar prefix caching?
[00:05:46] Priya (Redwood): Many vendors have basic caching. OpenAI's cache is more opaquely managed on API side; Anthropic folks have discussed similar KV caches, but Redwood's per-route, per-model instrumentation and prefix-specific canonicalization tooling is what we're highlighting.
[00:06:00] Alex (Redwood): Ok thanks everyone. Any final comments?
[00:06:03] Luis (Acme): No, thanks.
[00:06:04] Sana (Acme): Thanks, talk soon.
[00:06:06] Jared (Acme): Thanks.
[00:06:08] Priya (Redwood): Thanks all, we'll follow up in thread and push dashboard invite.
[00:06:12] Alex (Redwood): Meeting adjourned.

Notes: Timestamp cadence here is coarse at start; detailed instrumentation logs stored separately. Some transcription artifacts present (product names).
